<script>

function saveSvgFromParentDiv(divElId, downloadName) {
	var divSvgWrapperEl = document.getElementById(divElId);

	var svgEl = divSvgWrapperEl.firstElementChild;
  svgEl.setAttribute("xmlns", "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg");
  var svgData = svgEl.outerHTML;
  var preface = '<?xml version="1.0" standalone="no"?>\r\n';
  var svgBlob = new Blob([preface, svgData], {type:"image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8"});
  var svgUrl = URL.createObjectURL(svgBlob);
  
  _createThenClickImageLink(svgUrl, downloadName);
}

function saveSvgFromParentDiv2(clickedEl, downloadName) {

	var svgEl = clickedEl.previousElementSibling;
  svgEl.setAttribute("xmlns", "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg");
  var svgData = svgEl.outerHTML;
  var preface = '<?xml version="1.0" standalone="no"?>\r\n';
  var svgBlob = new Blob([preface, svgData], {type:"image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8"});
  var svgUrl = URL.createObjectURL(svgBlob);
  
  _createThenClickImageLink(svgUrl, downloadName);
}

function savePngFromParentDiv(clickedEl, downloadName) {
	var imgEl = clickedEl.previousElementSibling;
	
	_createThenClickImageLink(imgEl.src, downloadName);
}

function _createThenClickImageLink(imageUrl, downloadName) {
  var downloadLink = document.createElement("a");
  downloadLink.href = imageUrl;
  downloadLink.download = downloadName;
  
  document.body.appendChild(downloadLink);
  downloadLink.click(); // triggers image download
  document.body.removeChild(downloadLink);
}
</script>

```{r include=FALSE}
#message(params$quantif_file)

source("../../Library/quantitativeProteomics.R")

if(dir.exists("temp") == FALSE){
  dir.create("temp")
}

createPngOrSvg <- function(plot_data, image_name, height = 600, length = 600, grob=FALSE) {

  if (format_svg) {
    s <- svgstring()
    if (grob) {
      print(plot_data)
    } else {
      plot(plot_data)
    }
    invisible(dev.off())
    return(paste0("<div id='svgWrapper'>", s(),"<a class='no-print' href='javascript:void(0);' onclick=\"javascript:saveSvgFromParentDiv2(this,'",image_name,".svg');\" >Save figure</a></div>"))

  } else {
    png_file <- paste0("./temp/",image_name, ".png")
    png(filename = png_file, width = length, height = height, type = "cairo")
    if (grob) {
      print(plot_data)
    } else {
      plot(plot_data)
    }

    invisible(dev.off())
    png_binary <- readBin(png_file, what = "raw", n = file.info(png_file)$size)
    png_base64 <- base64encode(png_binary)

    return(paste0("<div id='pngWrapper'><img src='data:image/png;base64,",png_base64,"' ><a href='javascript:void(0);' onclick=\"javascript:savePngFromParentDiv(this, '",image_name,".png');\" >Save figure</a></div>"))

  }
}
```

```{r file_import, include=FALSE}
##Importing raw data file given as a parameter and parses the names of the samples included##

data <- read.csv(params$quantif_file, check.names = F, sep="\t")

# Condition and replicate of each sample (in the order of the sample columns), when an experimental design is given
sample_conditions <- NULL
sample_replicates <- NULL

if(file.exists(params$design_exp)){
  expDesign <- read.csv(params$design_exp, header = T, sep="\t")

  # Checking that the experimental design and the quantification table are consistent
  validate_inputs(data, expDesign, derived_suffixes = character(0))

  group_ids <- unique(expDesign$Condition)
  
  abundance_repbio = data.frame(data$Id)
  colnames(abundance_repbio) = "Id"
  
  identification_type_repbio = data.frame(data$Id)
  colnames(identification_type_repbio) = "Id"
  
  for(group in group_ids){
    
    sub = subset(expDesign,expDesign$Condition==group)
    
    for (rBio in unique(sub$repBio)){
      
      samples_intensities = subset(sub,sub$repBio==rBio)$File
      samples_identification_type = paste0("Identification_type",sub("Intensity","",samples_intensities))
      
      abundance_repbio = cbind(abundance_repbio,data[as.character(samples_intensities)])
      identification_type_repbio = cbind(identification_type_repbio,data[samples_identification_type])
      
      colnames(abundance_repbio)[ncol(abundance_repbio)] = paste0("Intensity_",sub(" ", "", rBio),"_",group)
      colnames(identification_type_repbio)[ncol(identification_type_repbio)] = paste0("Identification_type_",sub(" ", "", rBio),"_",group)
      sample_conditions <- c(sample_conditions, as.character(group))
      sample_replicates <- c(sample_replicates, as.character(rBio))
    }
  }
  
  data = merge.data.frame(data[, 1:3],identification_type_repbio,by="Id")
  data = merge.data.frame(data,abundance_repbio,by="Id")
}
sample_names = colnames(data)[grepl("Intensity",names(data))]
# Sample name without the intensity prefix, as in the identification type columns ("Identification_type_<sample>"):
# ("Intensity_<repBio>_<Condition>" with an experimental design, the input column names otherwise)
sample_names_parsed = sub("^Intensity_", "", sample_names)
parameters <- read.csv(params$parameters, header=T, sep="=")

# write.csv(data, "QC_data.csv", row.names = F)

```


```{r param_parsing}
# ##Parsing parameters##
# as.logical, as.numeric, as.character()
Normalization = as.logical(parameters["Normalization",])
keep_empty_rows = as.logical(parameters["keep_empty_rows",])
format_svg = as.logical(parameters["format_svg",])
coloring_by_group = as.logical(parameters["coloring_by_group",])

# Percentile (in %) of the observed intensities of each sample used as noise level by the imputation (5 if absent)
if ("Imputation.MNAR.percentile" %in% rownames(parameters)) {
  Imputation.MNAR.percentile = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(parameters["Imputation.MNAR.percentile",])))
} else {
  Imputation.MNAR.percentile = 5
  cat("Note: parameter Imputation.MNAR.percentile is absent, 5 is used.\n", file = stderr())
}
if (is.na(Imputation.MNAR.percentile) || Imputation.MNAR.percentile <= 0 || Imputation.MNAR.percentile > 10) {
  stop("Parameter Imputation.MNAR.percentile must be greater than 0 and at most 10 (%).")
}
```

```{r delete_empty_rows}
if(keep_empty_rows==FALSE){
  data$na_count = apply(data[grepl("Intensity",names(data))],1,function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
  data = subset(data,data$na_count!=ncol(data[grepl("Intensity",names(data))]))
}
```

```{r find group names}
##Parses sample group names from raw data file##

if(coloring_by_group && file.exists(params$design_exp)){
  
  color_group <- TRUE

  kable(expDesign,format="html",col.names = NULL,booktabs = T, caption = "Experimental design") %>%
          kable_styling(bootstrap_options="condensed",full_width = F,position = "left") %>%
          column_spec(1, bold = T)
  
  group_names <- unique(expDesign$Condition)

  ######################################################################
  
  l <- length(group_names)
  if(l <= 12){
    group_colors <- brewer.pal(l, "Paired")
  }else{
    group_colors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))(l)
  }
  
  ######################################################################
  
  # Colour of each sample: the colour of its group, in the order of the sample columns
  # (one sample per repBio of each condition, see sample_conditions)
  sample_colors <- group_colors[match(sample_conditions, group_names)]
}else{
  color_group <- FALSE
}

```


```{r colname_parsing, results='asis'}
##Parsing from data file the names of the samples and limits the length of sample names. If sample names > 15 characters, numbers will be used in## 
##the graphic keys##

max_lenght_sample_name = nchar(sample_names_parsed[nchar(sample_names_parsed)==max(nchar(sample_names_parsed))][1])

if (max_lenght_sample_name>15){
  if(file.exists(params$design_exp)){
    # "<Condition>_<index>": the samples (one per repBio of each condition, see sample_conditions) are numbered within their
    # condition, in the order of the columns, so that the names are unique whatever the order of the design rows
    sample_number <- paste0(sample_conditions, "_", ave(seq_along(sample_conditions), sample_conditions, FUN = seq_along))
  }else{
    # Without experimental design, the samples are numbered: S1, S2...
    sample_number = paste0("S", seq_along(sample_names))
  }
  setnames(data, old=as.character(sample_names),new=sample_number)
  sample_names = sample_number
  # Correspondence between the original and the short names
  cat(kable(data.frame(Sample = sample_names_parsed, Id = sample_number),format="html",caption="Samples id") %>% kable_styling() %>% scroll_box(height = "200px"))
}else{
  sample_number = sample_names_parsed
  setnames(data, old=as.character(sample_names),new=sample_names_parsed)
  sample_names = sample_names_parsed
}
namesDF = data.frame(sample_names_parsed,sample_number)
colnames(namesDF)=c("Sample","Id")
```

```{r log_transformation}
colnames(log_abundance) = sample_names
```

```{r bar graph, results='asis'}
# Total intensity of each sample: sum of all its observed intensities, before normalization
TotalIntensitiesDF <- data.frame(
  sample = factor(sample_names, levels = sample_names),
  total_intensity = sapply(sample_names, function(s) sum(as.numeric(data[[s]]), na.rm = TRUE)),
  row.names = NULL)

# Bars sorted by total intensity. The colours follow the sample (factor levels in the order of sample_names), not the row order
TotalIntensitiesDF <- TotalIntensitiesDF[order(TotalIntensitiesDF$total_intensity), ]

# Creating ggplot bar graph

M_intensity_comparison <- ggplot(data = TotalIntensitiesDF) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity",aes(x=sample, y=total_intensity, fill = sample))+
  scale_x_discrete(limits = as.character(TotalIntensitiesDF$sample)) +
  ggtitle("Total intensity across runs") +
  ylab("Total intensity")+
  xlab("")+
  {if(color_group) scale_fill_manual(values = sample_colors)} +
  theme(legend.position="none",
        plot.title = element_text(size=22),
        axis.title=element_text(size=18),
        axis.text=element_text(size=18),
        axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90))

##Plotting and printing 'Intensity distribution in each sample' violin plot into html (.svg or .png dependent on set parameters) with download link##

cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(M_intensity_comparison,"Total_intensity_across_runs")))
figure_note("Total intensity of each sample (sum of all its observed intensities) before normalization, sorted from the lowest to the highest. It shows the differences of total measured signal between samples: a sample with a lower total can come from a lower protein amount (biological sample collection), a sample preparation issue or a loss of sensitivity of the mass spectrometer. It also decreases with the number of proteins quantified, and is dominated by the most abundant proteins. Moderate differences are corrected by the normalization.")
```

```{r correlation_plot, results='asis'}
##If the number of samples < 16 AND the data for each sample is < 5000 rows, a scatterplot of pairwise comparisons is framed##
##Else, a heatplot of correlated coefficients is framed##

if (length(sample_names)<16 & nrow(data)<5000){
  correlogram = ggpairs(log_abundance,title="Sample correlation",upper=list(continuous=wrap("cor",size=3)),lower=list(continuous=wrap("points",size=0.15))) +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 6),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 6),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 22))
}else{
  cormat <- round(cor(log_abundance,use = "complete.obs"),2)
  #cormat = melt(cormat)
  cormat <- reshape2::melt(cormat)
  colnames(cormat) = c("Samples1","Samples2","Coefficient")
  # Sample label size decreasing with the number of samples, so that the labels do not overlap (18 up to 16 samples, 7 for 40)
  label_size <- max(5, min(18, 290 / length(sample_names)))
  correlogram = ggplot(data = cormat, aes(x=Samples1, y=Samples2, fill=Coefficient)) +
    geom_tile() +
    # Sequential scale over the observed coefficients (white = lowest, red = 1), so that the outlier samples stand out
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "red") +
    xlab("")+
    ylab("")+
    ggtitle("Sample correlation") +
    labs(fill = "Correlation coefficient") +
    theme(plot.title=element_text(size=22),
        axis.title=element_text(size=18),
        axis.text.y=element_text(size=label_size),
        axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, hjust=1, vjust=0.5, size=label_size),
        legend.title=element_text(size=16),
        legend.text = element_text(size=16))
}

##Plotting and printing the 'sample correlation' plot into html (.svg or .png dependent on set parameters) with download link##

cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(correlogram,"Sample_correlation", grob=TRUE)))
if (length(sample_names)<16 & nrow(data)<5000){
  figure_note("Pairwise comparison of the samples on the log10 intensities: scatter plots (below the diagonal), Pearson correlation coefficients (above) and intensity distributions (diagonal). Replicates of the same condition should have the highest correlations; a sample less correlated with all the others is a possible outlier.")
} else {
  figure_note("Pearson correlation coefficients between the samples, computed on the log10 intensities of the proteins quantified in every sample (white: lowest coefficient, red: 1). Replicates of the same condition should have the highest correlations; a light row and column point to a sample less correlated with all the others, a possible outlier.")
}
```

```{r identification_type_plot, results='asis'}

## Number of proteins identified (by MS/MS) and quantified (by MS/MS or by matching) in each sample ##

identification_type = data[,grepl("Identification_type_",names(data)), drop = FALSE]

if(ncol(identification_type)>0){

  # Short sample name of each identification type column (same order as the sample columns)
  id_samples <- sapply(colnames(identification_type), function(col) as.character(namesDF$Id[namesDF$Sample == sub("^Identification_type_", "", col)]))

  # Counts per sample, among the proteins quantified in the sample (with an intensity): identified = by MS/MS, the others are
  # quantified without MS/MS identification. The identification type alone is not used for "quantified", as it can be given
  # for a protein without intensity (e.g. Proline derives it from the PSM count).
  quantified <- sapply(id_samples, function(s) { x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(data[[s]])); !is.na(x) & x > 0 })
  msms <- as.matrix(identification_type) == "By MS/MS"
  msms[is.na(msms)] <- FALSE
  id_counts <- data.frame(
    sample = factor(id_samples, levels = id_samples),
    msms = colSums(quantified & msms),
    total = colSums(quantified),
    row.names = NULL)
  id_counts$other <- id_counts$total - id_counts$msms

  # One row per sample and type for the stacked bars (identified by MS/MS at the bottom)
  id_long <- rbind(data.frame(sample = id_counts$sample, type = "Identified (by MS/MS)", count = id_counts$msms),
                   data.frame(sample = id_counts$sample, type = "Quantified without MS/MS identification", count = id_counts$other))
  id_long$type <- factor(id_long$type, levels = c("Quantified without MS/MS identification", "Identified (by MS/MS)"))
  id_type_colors <- c("Identified (by MS/MS)" = "dodgerblue4", "Quantified without MS/MS identification" = "dodgerblue1")

  # Condition of each sample, when an experimental design is given (a colored mark under each bar)
  id_has_design <- length(sample_conditions) == nrow(id_counts)
  if (id_has_design) id_counts$condition <- factor(sample_conditions, levels = unique(sample_conditions))
  id_max <- max(id_counts$total)

  # Smaller labels when there are many samples, so that they do not overlap
  n_id_samples <- nrow(id_counts)
  id_label_size <- if (n_id_samples > 20) 11 else 16
  id_count_size <- if (n_id_samples > 20) 2.6 else 4

  identification_type_plot = ggplot(id_long, aes(x = sample, y = count)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = type), width = 0.9) +
    scale_fill_manual("", values = id_type_colors, breaks = rev(names(id_type_colors))) +
    # Number identified by MS/MS, inside the MS/MS segment, and number quantified, above the bar
    geom_text(data = id_counts, aes(x = sample, y = msms, label = msms), angle = 90, hjust = 1.1, colour = "white", size = id_count_size) +
    geom_text(data = id_counts, aes(x = sample, y = total, label = total), angle = 90, hjust = -0.1, colour = "grey20", size = id_count_size) +
    {if (id_has_design) geom_point(data = id_counts, aes(x = sample, y = -0.03 * id_max, colour = condition), shape = 15, size = 3)} +
    {if (id_has_design && color_group) scale_colour_manual("Condition", values = setNames(group_colors, group_names))} +
    {if (id_has_design) labs(colour = "Condition")} +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.1))) +
    xlab("") +
    ylab("Number of proteins") +
    ggtitle("Identified and quantified proteins per sample") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size=22),
          axis.title=element_text(size=18),
          axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, hjust=1, vjust=0.5, size=id_label_size),
          axis.text.y=element_text(size=16),
          legend.position="bottom",
          legend.box="vertical",
          legend.title=element_text(size=16),
          legend.text=element_text(size=16))

  cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(identification_type_plot,"Identification_types_distribution_across_samples", 650, max(600, 22 * n_id_samples))))
  cat(text_spec(paste0("\n Number of proteins quantified in each sample (with an intensity: bar height, number above the bar), and among them the proteins ",
                       "identified by MS/MS in that sample (dark blue, number inside the bar). The others (light blue) are quantified without MS/MS identification ",
                       "in the sample (e.g. by matching). A sample with clearly fewer identifications than the other samples of its condition may indicate a problem with that injection.",
                       if (id_has_design) " The colored mark under each bar gives the condition of the sample." else ""),
                italic = T, font_size = "12px"))
}
```

```{r normalization}

##Parsing from data file for normalization of samples##

na_count_by_sample = unname(colSums(is.na(as.matrix(data[,sample_names]))))
na_by_sample = data.frame(na_count_by_sample,sample_names)

# Extract raw intensities
raw_abundance = data[sample_names]

if (Normalization){
  
  # Find the sample with less NA
  reference_sample = subset(na_by_sample,na_by_sample$na_count_by_sample==min(na_by_sample$na_count_by_sample))$sample_names[1]
  
  # Normalization
  intensities_to_normalize = cbind(data$Id,raw_abundance)
  colnames(intensities_to_normalize)[1] = "Id"
  normalized_abundance = normalize(intensities_to_normalize,reference_sample)
  
  data = cbind(data,normalized_abundance[,-1])
  
  pattern = "_norm"
  
}else{
  
  pattern = ""
}
```

```{r missing_values_imputation, results='asis'}
##Checks if normalized abundance data exists##

if(exists('normalized_abundance') && is.data.frame(get('normalized_abundance'))){
  data_to_impute = cbind.data.frame(data$Id,normalized_abundance)
}else{
  data_to_impute = cbind.data.frame(data$Id,raw_abundance)
}

##Creating data frame for 'Log intensities distribution with imputed values' histogram##

# Imputation with the noise model of the library (see estimate_noise_model). The noise sd is estimated within conditions when an
# experimental design is given, and over all the samples (one group) otherwise. If the model cannot be estimated (too few
# low-intensity proteins), the missing values are replaced by the percentile of each sample.
has_design_for_imputation <- length(sample_conditions) == ncol(data_to_impute) - 1
imputation_groups <- if (has_design_for_imputation) sample_conditions else rep("all samples", ncol(data_to_impute) - 1)
percentile <- Imputation.MNAR.percentile/100

noise_model <- tryCatch(estimate_noise_model(data_to_impute, imputation_groups, percentile), error = function(e) e)
if (inherits(noise_model, "error")) {
  imputed_samples = impute_using_noise_percentile(data_to_impute, percentile)
  imputation_text <- paste0("Missing values are replaced by the ", Imputation.MNAR.percentile, "% percentile of the observed intensities of each sample (the noise model could not be estimated: ",
                            sub("\\.$", "", sub("^Imputation: ", "", sub(" Use the percentile model.*$", "", conditionMessage(noise_model)))), ").")
} else {
  imputed_samples = impute_using_noise_model(data_to_impute, imputation_groups, noise_model, seed = 1)
  imputation_text <- paste0("Missing values are imputed with the noise model: values are drawn around the noise level of each sample (the ",
                            Imputation.MNAR.percentile, "% percentile of its observed intensities) with a standard deviation of ",
                            formatC(noise_model$noise_sd, format = "f", digits = 2), " log2, estimated on ", noise_model$n_rows, " low-intensity protein measurements ",
                            ifelse(has_design_for_imputation, "within conditions.", "over all the samples taken as one group (no experimental design was given, so the standard deviation may include differences between conditions)."),
                            " The imputation uses a fixed seed and is reproducible.")
}
data = cbind(data,imputed_samples)

#####imputed_samples_log = imputed_samples

#####imputed_samples_log[,1:ncol(imputed_samples_log)] = log10(imputed_samples_log)
imputed_samples_log <- imputed_samples
imputed_samples_log[imputed_samples_log == 0] <- 1e-8
imputed_samples_log <- log10(imputed_samples_log)

colnames(imputed_samples_log)[1:ncol(imputed_samples_log)] = paste0(colnames(imputed_samples_log)[1:ncol(imputed_samples_log)],"_log")
data = cbind(data,imputed_samples_log)

# Make a data frame of values to plot
imputed_abundance = data[,grepl("_imputed_log",names(data)), drop = FALSE]
imputedIntensityDF = reshape2::melt(imputed_abundance)
colnames(imputedIntensityDF) = c("sample","log10_intensity")
imputedIntensityDF$sample = sub("_imputed_log","",imputedIntensityDF$sample)

# Build NA mask from raw_abundance for the SAME sample columns (and same order)
raw_mat <- raw_abundance[, sample_names, drop = FALSE]         # exclude Id
na_mask <- is.na(raw_mat)

# Melt mask and attach (same ordering if columns align)
imputedFlagDF <- reshape2::melt(na_mask)
imputedIntensityDF$imputed <- imputedFlagDF$value

## imputed? (one flag per protein and sample, in the same order as reshape2::melt(imputed_abundance), i.e. sample by sample)
imputed = as.vector(na_mask)
## final dataframe
#imputedIntensityDF <- data.frame(imputedIntensityDF,imputed)


##Framing 'Log intensities distribution with imputed values' histogram using ggplot##
histogram <- ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(data = imputedIntensityDF, mapping = aes(x = log10_intensity, fill = imputed), alpha=0.7, bins = 100) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("dodgerblue3", "darkorchid4"))+
  ggtitle("Log intensities distribution with imputed values") +
  xlab("log(intensity)")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size=22),
        axis.title=element_text(size=18),
        axis.text=element_text(size=18),
        legend.title = element_text(size=16),
        legend.text = element_text(size=16))

##Plotting and printing 'Log intensities distribution with imputed values' histogram to html doc (.svg or .png dependent on set parameters)##
##with download link##

  htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(histogram,"Log_intensities_distribution_with_imputed_values"))

##Prints explanation of histogram data##

cat(text_spec(paste0("\n ", imputation_text),italic=T,font_size="12px"))
```

```{r pca_compute, echo=FALSE}
## PCA of the samples: samples are the observations, proteins the variables ##

# Log10 intensities after normalization (if enabled) and imputation, one column per sample
pca_matrix <- as.matrix(imputed_abundance)
colnames(pca_matrix) <- sample_names

# Values that were missing before imputation, and number of quantified proteins per sample (proteome depth)
missing_before_imputation <- is.na(as.matrix(raw_abundance[sample_names]))
n_quantified <- colSums(!missing_before_imputation)
pct_imputed <- round(100 * mean(missing_before_imputation), 1)

# Main PCA: each protein centered, not scaled (more variable proteins weigh more)
pca_main <- compute_sample_pca(pca_matrix)

# Scaled PCA: each protein centered and scaled to unit variance (every protein weighs the same)
pca_scaled <- compute_sample_pca(pca_matrix, scale = TRUE)

# Proteins with a non-finite value are left out of the PCA (see compute_sample_pca)
pca_matrix <- pca_matrix[apply(pca_matrix, 1, function(x) all(is.finite(x))), , drop = FALSE]
pca_subtitle <- paste0(pca_main$n_proteins, " proteins, ", pct_imputed, "% of the values imputed")

# Sample annotations (condition and replicate are known only when an experimental design is given)
pca_samples <- data.frame(sample = sample_names, n_quantified = n_quantified, row.names = NULL)
has_design <- length(sample_conditions) == length(sample_names)
if (has_design) {
  pca_samples$condition <- factor(sample_conditions, levels = unique(sample_conditions))
  pca_samples$replicate <- factor(sample_replicates, levels = unique(sample_replicates))
}

# Colors of the conditions (variance_explained and plot_pca_samples are in the library)
pca_colors <- if (color_group) setNames(group_colors, group_names) else NULL

```

Their technical noise then has as much weight as the biological changes: this view helps to detect technical effects (injection order, batches), not biological ones.", italic = T, font_size = "12px"))

```{r pca_depth, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
## Do the first components follow the proteome depth of the samples? ##

depth_df <- rbind(
  data.frame(pca_samples, component = "PC1", score = pca_main$x[, 1]),
  data.frame(pca_samples, component = "PC2", score = pca_main$x[, 2])
)
depth_r <- c(PC1 = cor(pca_main$x[, 1], n_quantified), PC2 = cor(pca_main$x[, 2], n_quantified))
depth_df$component <- factor(depth_df$component, levels = c("PC1", "PC2"),
                             labels = paste0(c("PC1", "PC2"), " (r = ", round(depth_r, 2), ")"))

depth_plot <- ggplot(depth_df, aes(x = n_quantified, y = score)) +
  {if (has_design) geom_point(aes(colour = condition), size = 3) else geom_point(size = 3)} +
  {if (has_design && color_group) scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(group_colors, group_names))} +
  facet_wrap(~component, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Components vs proteome depth", x = "Number of quantified proteins (before imputation)", y = "Sample score") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 20),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12))

htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(depth_plot, "PCA_vs_proteome_depth", 700, 700))
cat(text_spec("\n Sample scores of the main PCA against the number of proteins quantified in each sample. A strong correlation (|r| close to 1) means that the component mostly reflects differences in proteome depth (and therefore imputed values) rather than biology.", italic = T, font_size = "12px"))
```

```{r pca_scree, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
## Variance explained by the first components of both PCAs ##

n_components <- min(10, length(pca_main$sdev))
scree_df <- rbind(
  data.frame(pca = "Main PCA", component = seq_len(n_components), variance = variance_explained(pca_main)[seq_len(n_components)]),
  data.frame(pca = "Proteins scaled", component = seq_len(n_components), variance = variance_explained(pca_scaled)[seq_len(n_components)])
)

scree_plot <- ggplot(scree_df, aes(x = factor(component), y = variance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "dodgerblue3") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(variance, 1), "%")), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(~pca, ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(title = "Variance explained", x = "Component", y = "% of variance") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 20),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14))

cat(htmltools::HTML(createPngOrSvg(scree_plot, "PCA_variance_explained", 700, 700)))
figure_note("Percentage of the variance of the samples explained by each of the first components, for both PCAs. A first component well above the others means that one main effect (e.g. the conditions, or a technical effect) dominates the differences between samples.")
```

```{r pca_top_loadings, echo=FALSE}
## Proteins contributing most to the first two components of the main PCA ##

# Protein labels: gene name when available, accession otherwise
protein_labels <- as.character(data$Id)
if ("Accession" %in% colnames(data)) protein_labels <- as.character(data$Accession)
if ("Gene_name" %in% colnames(data)) {
  has_gene <- !is.na(data$Gene_name) & data$Gene_name != ""
  protein_labels[has_gene] <- as.character(data$Gene_name[has_gene])
}
names(protein_labels) <- rownames(imputed_abundance)
loadings_labels <- protein_labels[rownames(pca_matrix)]

top_loadings <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("PC1", "PC2"), function(pc) {
  l <- pca_main$rotation[, pc]
  top <- order(abs(l), decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(10, length(l)))]
  data.frame(Component = pc, Rank = seq_along(top), Protein = loadings_labels[top], Loading = round(l[top], 3), row.names = NULL)
}))

kable(top_loadings, format = "html", booktabs = T,
      caption = "Proteins with the largest loadings on PC1 and PC2 of the main PCA (the sign gives the direction along the component)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "condensed", full_width = F, position = "left") %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top")
```

```{r heatmaps, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='asis'}
    scale_x_continuous(name = "Proteins", breaks = NULL, labels = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(title = "Log Intensities Heatmap") +
    theme(#axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.title.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      plot.title=element_text(size=30),
      axis.title=element_text(size=25),
      axis.text.y=element_text(size=12),
      axis.text.x=element_text(angle = 90),
      legend.text=element_text(size=16),
      legend.title=element_text(size=18))

matrixGrob <- ggplotGrob(hcPlot)

#Make dendrogram plots
dendrogramSamples <- dendro_data(hClustSamples, type="rectangle")
dendrogramDataSamples <- segment(dendrogramSamples)
dendrogramSamplesPlot <- ggplot() +
    geom_segment(data = dendrogramDataSamples, mapping = aes(x=x, y=y, xend=xend, yend=yend)) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_y_reverse(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    #scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    #scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0.5, 6.5)) +
    theme(axis.line = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          axis.text = element_blank(),
          axis.title = element_blank(),
          panel.background = element_blank(),
          panel.grid = element_blank(),
          panel.border = element_blank())
dendroSampleGrob <- ggplotGrob(dendrogramSamplesPlot)

diff_cols <- ncol(matrixGrob) - ncol(dendroSampleGrob)

if (diff_cols > 0) {
  dendroSampleGrob <- gtable_add_cols(dendroSampleGrob, unit(rep(1, ncol(matrixGrob) - ncol(dendroSampleGrob)), "null"), pos = -1)
}

# result <- rbind(dendroSampleGrob[7, ], matrixGrob[7:nrow(matrixGrob), ], size = "last")
# result <- rbind(matrixGrob[1:6, ], result, size = "last")
result <- cbind(dendroSampleGrob[, 5], matrixGrob[, 5:ncol(matrixGrob)], size = "last")
result <- cbind(matrixGrob[, 1:4], result, size = "last")
result$heights[7] <- unit(0.2, "null")
result$widths[5] <- unit(0.2, "null")

# write.csv(heatmapDF, "heatmapDF.csv")

imputed_abundance_Z <- t(scale(t(imputed_abundance)))
heatmapDF_Z = reshape2::melt(imputed_abundance_Z)
heatmapDF_Z <- heatmapDF_Z[-1]
colnames(heatmapDF_Z)[1] <- "variable"

heatmapDF_Z$variable = sub(paste0(pattern,"_imputed_log"),"",heatmapDF_Z$variable)
heatmapDF_Z = cbind(heatmapDF_Z,proteinRank,imputed)
colnames(heatmapDF_Z) = c("sample","log_intensity","proteinRank","imputed")

heatmapDF_Z=subset(heatmapDF_Z,heatmapDF_Z$imputed==F)

# Order samples according to clustering results
orderedSamples <- sample_names[hClustSamples$order]
orderedSamples <- orderedSamples[!is.na(orderedSamples)]
# (keep the clustering order, so that the rows match the dendrogram)
heatmapDF_Z$orderedSamples <- factor(heatmapDF_Z$sample, levels = orderedSamples)
heatmapDF_Z$x <- as.numeric(heatmapDF_Z$orderedSamples)

# Order proteins according to clustering results
heatmapDF_Z$orderedProteins <- factor(heatmapDF_Z$proteinRank, levels = hClustProteins$order)
heatmapDF_Z$y <- as.numeric(heatmapDF_Z$orderedProteins)

# Adjust colors
minRatio <- min(heatmapDF_Z$log_intensity)
maxRatio <- max(heatmapDF_Z$log_intensity)
maxabsRatio <- max(abs(heatmapDF_Z$log_intensity))

hcPlot_scored <- ggplot(data = heatmapDF_Z) +
    geom_raster(mapping = aes(x = y, y = x, fill = log_intensity)) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colours=c("green","yellow","red")) +
    #scale_fill_scico(palette = "berlin") +
    ggtitle("")+
    scale_y_continuous(name = "Sample", breaks = 1:length(orderedSamples), labels = orderedSamples, expand = c(0, 0), position = "right") +
    scale_x_continuous(name = "Proteins", breaks = NULL, labels = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(title = "Z-Scored Log Intensities Heatmap") +
    theme(#axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.title.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      plot.title=element_text(size=30),
      axis.title=element_text(size=25),
      axis.text.y=element_text(size=12),
      axis.text.x=element_text(angle = 90),
      legend.text=element_text(size=16),
      legend.title=element_text(size=18))

matrixGrob_scored <- ggplotGrob(hcPlot_scored)

#Make dendrogram plots
dendrogramSamples_scored <- dendro_data(hClustSamples, type="rectangle")
dendrogramDataSamples_scored <- segment(dendrogramSamples_scored)

    # scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0.5, 6.5)) +
    theme(axis.line = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks = element_blank(),
          axis.text = element_blank(),
          axis.title = element_blank(),
          panel.background = element_blank(),
          panel.grid = element_blank(),
          panel.border = element_blank())
dendroSampleGrob_scored <- ggplotGrob(dendrogramSamplesPlot_scored)

if (diff_cols_scored > 0) {
  dendroSampleGrob_scored <- gtable_add_cols(dendroSampleGrob_scored, unit(rep(1, ncol(matrixGrob_scored) - ncol(dendroSampleGrob_scored)), "null"), pos = -1)
}
```
